html:
A round bronze coin with a square hole, first cast in 621 by the founder of the Tang dynasty in China. It set the pattern for East Asian coins for almost thirteen hundred years.

It replaced the wuzhu coins used since the Han dynasty. The four characters on its face mean roughly "circulating treasure of the new beginning". Its weight became a standard unit, and coins after it were named in the same way, with "tongbao" or "zhongbao", until the end of the empire in 1912.

Neighbours copied it. Japan's first coins of the early 700s followed its size and style, and Korea and Vietnam made similar coins. Strings of these coins, a thousand to a string, paid taxes and wages. Under the Song, the need to carry so many heavy coins helped lead to paper money such as the jiaozi.
